WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (term_premium_lapse_and_conversion), revision 2 after the policy-task audit.
[Step 0 draw] prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[4,5,6,4]: advance (root) 6, reinstatement 5, billing 4, rider ending 4.
[Why a good test] Lorraine asks only to be paid her approved terminal illness advance; 'The advance is paid only once the policy status on record has returned from lapsed to in force.' Her policy lapsed on 2026-06-02. Reinstating needs her own payment, fixed only after the ledger carries the 2026-08-01 installment that fell due while lapsed; that back installment is billed at the premium in effect on its due date, without the accidental death charge (age 70 at the 2026-08-01 anniversary). After reinstatement the rider is removed so the installment on record is right, because the lien includes the premium set aside at that installment, less the months already paid ahead to 2026-11-01.
[Scope] claims term_ext_lapse_installment_billing, term_ext_reinstatement_collection, term_ext_adb_expiry_repricing, term_ext_accelerated_lien; tools bill_back_installment_903386f9, pay_reinstatement_amount_3f8d4404 (owner=user), end_expired_adb_rider_b05b3f4a, pay_accelerated_advance_7c43a05b. Disjoint from task 0.
[Problem-tree card] root term_ext_accelerated_lien; edges advance<-reinstatement (state_gate acceleration_status), advance<-rider ending (value_input premium_set_aside), rider ending<-reinstatement (state_gate rider_change_status), reinstatement<-billing (value_input back_premium). Deletion runs: skip billing -> reinstatement 286.34 (gold 533.29); skip rider ending -> lien 104,903.47 (gold 104,874.85); skip reinstatement -> status stays lapsed. Unique chain order.
[Base-invariant card] within_reinstatement_window: lapse 2026-06-02 + 60 months = 2031-06-02, signed 2026-06-25; approved_application; rider_change_status and acceleration_status in force after step 12; approved_acceleration_claim, life expectancy 8 <= 12.
[Business-object card] policy LT10917346; back premium rows billed 2024-08-01..2026-05-01 at 260.07 less 7 check payments; completed reinstatements 2022-04-05 (counted) and 2019-05-10 (near-miss, 87 months); whole life WL10734402 (600,000) with its 400,000 advance of 2026-03-20 under whole claim (completed, now seeded); no UL. The reinstatement application's evidence_type 'none' covers lapse gaps of 0-31 days, which spans the 15-day cut of both the rate and the interest-day ladders, so it names neither tier.

user_scenario: You are Lorraine A. Petrakis, 70, a retired school librarian in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, who owns an Ashgrove Level Term 25 policy on her own life. You are seriously ill; you speak softly, politely and precisely, and you tire easily, so you keep your answers short. You are calling because Ashgrove approved your claim for the terminal illness advance on your term policy and you want the advance paid to you now. Open with something like: "My claim for the early payout on my term life policy was approved, and I'd like the advance paid out to me, please." You give your telephone number, 6145550162, when first asked who you are. Only when asked to confirm your identity do you give, one at a time as asked, your date of birth, 1956-06-10, the last four of your Social Security number, 2417, and your ZIP code, 15217. If asked how much you asked for on the claim, you say $150,000; if told you can receive less than that under the rules, you accept it quietly. If asked about your doctor's estimate, you say it is on the certificate you sent and you would rather not discuss it. If asked whether you hold other policies with Ashgrove, you say you have a whole life policy with them, on which you already received an advance this spring, and a universal life policy that lapsed years ago. If asked how the advance should be paid, you say by direct deposit to the bank account they already have. You do not know your premium, the amount of any charge, or any figure the rules produce, and you never offer or guess one. Only if the representative tells you that a payment is needed on your policy before the advance can be paid, you agree, and when the representative hands the payment step over to you, you pay exactly the amount the representative names from your bank's online bill pay, and read back the confirmation you receive. If the representative tells you a rider has come off the policy or your premium has changed, you accept it without questions. Once the representative tells you the advance has been paid and what lien it places on the policy, you thank them and end the call.
